facts.fact_text: The applicants were mainly questioned about their participation in a number of demonstrations.
All the applicants accepted that they had participated in legally organised demonstrations.
The applicants denied having chanted illegal slogans or slogans in favour of an illegal organisation during the demonstrations.

In the indictment, the Ankara public prosecutor noted that the applicants had participated in a demonstration organised by trade unions and non-governmental organisations held on 17 December 2005 with the authorisation of the governor's office.

In the indictment, the Ankara public prosecutor noted that the applicants had participated in a demonstration organised by trade unions and non-governmental organisations held on 19 February 2006 with the authorisation of the governor's office.
On 6 March 2006 the applicants were taken into police custody.
The applicants were taken into police custody on suspicion of aiding and abetting the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party).
On 7 March 2006 the applicants were brought before a judge at the Ankara Assize Court.

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Deniz Bakır of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Metin Kürekçi of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Necla Çomak of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

On 17 January 2007 the Ankara Assize Court convicted Alihan Alhan of membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 7 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.
Metin Kürekçi was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Necla Çomak was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Alihan Alhan was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Deniz Bakır was sentenced to seven years and six months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.

The remaining applicants (other than Deniz Bakır, Metin Kürekçi, Necla Çomak and Alihan Alhan) were convicted on 17 January 2007 of disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation under section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).

The remaining applicants convicted of disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation were each sentenced to one year and eight months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
The applicants were charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 220 § 7 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).
The applicants were charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 314 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).

At the material time, Article 220 § 7 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provided that anyone who aids an illegal organisation knowingly and willingly, even if he does not belong to the hierarchical structure of the organisation, shall be punished as a member of the organisation.

At the material time, Article 220 § 8 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provided that anyone who spreads propaganda for the organisation or its objectives shall be punished by a term of imprisonment of between one and three years, and if the crime is committed through the press or other media, the sentence shall be increased by one half.

Between 7 August 2003 and 18 July 2006, section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 (Prevention of Terrorism Act) provided that any person who assists members of terrorist organisations or who disseminates propaganda inciting others to violence or other methods of terrorism shall be liable to a term of imprisonment of one to five years and a judicial fine of five million liras to one billion liras.

The first sentence of section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 (Prevention of Terrorism Act) was amended by Law no. 5532, which entered into force on 18 July 2006, to read: 'Any person who disseminates propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation shall be liable to a term of imprisonment of one to five years.'
The MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party) was classified as an illegal armed organisation.

In the indictment, the Ankara public prosecutor noted, on the basis of video footage provided by the police, that the applicants had carried banners on behalf of the ESP (the Socialist Platform of the Oppressed).

In the indictment, the Ankara public prosecutor noted, on the basis of video footage provided by the police, that the applicants had carried banners on behalf of the SGD (Socialist Youth Association).
According to information on the Internet, the ESP (the Socialist Platform of the Oppressed) and the SGD (Socialist Youth Association) were connected to the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party).

In its judgment, the Ankara Assize Court noted that although the ESP (Socialist Platform of the Oppressed) and the SGD (Socialist Youth Association) were legal entities, their activities were in line with those of the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party).

The Ankara Assize Court observed that members of the ESP (Socialist Platform of the Oppressed) and SGD (Socialist Youth Association) regarded members of the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party) who had been killed by the security forces as 'martyrs' and had organised commemorative ceremonies for them.

The Ankara Assize Court observed that members of the ESP (Socialist Platform of the Oppressed) and SGD (Socialist Youth Association) regarded members of the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party) who had died during hunger strikes as 'martyrs' and had organised commemorative ceremonies for them.

The Ankara Assize Court observed that the declarations issued by the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party) on the Internet were consistent with the aims of the ESP (Socialist Platform of the Oppressed) and the SGD (Socialist Youth Association).

The Ankara Assize Court considered that the ESP (Socialist Platform of the Oppressed) and the SGD (Socialist Youth Association) appeared in the legal domain on behalf of the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party) and had an organic relationship with it.

The Ankara Assize Court found it established, on the basis of the conduct of members of the ESP (Socialist Platform of the Oppressed) and the SGD (Socialist Youth Association) and having regard to the documents found in the accused's homes, that ESP and SGD members were carrying out activities in line with the strategies of the MLKP (Marxist-Leninist Communist Party).
All the applicants accepted that they had participated in legally organised demonstrations.
The applicants denied having chanted illegal slogans or slogans in favour of an illegal organisation during the demonstrations.
The applicants claimed that the material found in their homes had not been illegal.
Necla Çomak claimed that the documents found in her home were related to a legal association, namely the Working Women's Association (Emekçi Kadınlar Derneği).
Metin Kürekçi was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Necla Çomak was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Alihan Alhan was sentenced to six years and three months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.
Deniz Bakır was sentenced to seven years and six months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.

The remaining applicants (other than Deniz Bakır, Metin Kürekçi, Necla Çomak and Alihan Alhan) were convicted on 17 January 2007 of disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation under section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).

The remaining applicants convicted of disseminating propaganda in favour of a terrorist organisation were each sentenced to one year and eight months' imprisonment by the Ankara Assize Court on 17 January 2007.

The Court of Cassation quashed the judgment on the ground that the applicants had not had an opportunity to submit their defence submissions in relation to the classification by the Ankara Assize Court of their acts under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 (Prevention of Terrorism Act).
On 24 December 2009 the Court of Cassation upheld the Ankara Assize Court's judgment of 22 October 2008.

The Human Rights Watch report of 1 November 2010 stated that Turkish Penal Code Articles 220/6 and 220/7 are so vaguely worded and lacking in clarity about what is prohibited as to offer an individual no indication of how to regulate or limit conduct.

The Amnesty International report of 27 March 2013 stated that no inference should be drawn from someone undertaking a lawful act, such as participating in a peaceful demonstration, even if such acts benefit, through lawful means, goals shared by a terrorist organisation.
